data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["The Scottish Pride example is an explicit logical fallacy, whereas the decentralization argument often stems from the practical difficulty of enumerating all dependencies rather than deliberate fallacious reasoning."],"overturn_conditions":["A formal, pre-registered metric for 'independence' is adopted and used to evaluate the claim prospectively.","Proponents of the claim agree on a specific, observable failure mode that would definitively falsify it without redefining terms."],"shared_structure":["Retroactive exclusion of disconfirming evidence based on a newly discovered shared trait","Unfalsifiable core hypothesis protected by shifting the definition of the subject post hoc"],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_003"],"transfer_claims":["Any argument for decentralization based on 'independent operation' must be rejected unless independence is defined a priori with observable metrics.","Post-hoc discovery of shared causes in decentralized failures does not weaken the original claim, rendering the original claim useless for prediction."]},"claim":"The claim that decentralization provides superior correlated-failure resilience is unfalsifiable as typically stated, because 'independent operation' is operationally defined post hoc by the absence of observed correlation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A pre-registered, time-stamped inventory of all dependencies and environmental factors is available, preventing post-hoc rationalization of discovered correlations.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The hypothesis is explicitly limited to a narrow, pre-defined class of failures (e.g., internal software bugs) rather than general resilience.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When a decentralized network fails simultaneously, observers naturally look for a shared cause. Finding any shared cause (e.g., a common library, a shared cloud region, or a shared external shock) retroactively disqualifies the nodes from being 'truly independent'. This creates a protective ring around the hypothesis: if no failure occurs, the network is deemed resilient; if a failure occurs, the nodes are deemed not truly independent. Because the definition of independence excludes the very correlations that would disprove the hypothesis, the claim is structurally immune to falsification and thus meaningless for comparative resilience analysis without an independent, pre-registered metric for independence.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
